key_idea: Pair polynomially weighted edge cycles of K_n under a skew intersection form corrected by the rotation orders at vertices. The form vanishes on cycles, and interpolation-weighted polynomial tests then force the span of independent-edge evaluations at crossing pairs to have dimension at least C(s,2)^2, so the number of crossings is bounded below by a linear-algebra rank argument.
reason: Recasting the crossing count as a rank lower bound for a nondegenerate form that the cycle-pairing identity forces to vanish is striking. Combined with Lagrange interpolation weights and two-triangle interpolation patterns, it gives a conceptual route to an exact extremal result. The argument still carries a lot of technical bookkeeping: the local chord and shift construction in Lemma 2, the inductive interpolation lemma, the divisibility and minimal-degree descent, and a parity case split in the upper-bound count.
recognized: no — this claims Hill's conjecture (Guy–Harary–Hill Z(n)); the upper bound is the known two-page construction (Blažek–Koman / Damiani et al. / de Klerk–Pasechnik–Salazar), but I do not recognise the lower-bound proof
